text:
Alex Laferriere is getting a bigger job in Los Angeles: more than 20 minutes a night over his last ten games, and the ice for 70% of the Kings' power-play time, up from 30% last season. His own chances have jumped too, to 1.42 expected goals per 60 from 0.96.

That's a breakout in role. The goals haven't followed: three on 7.3 expected, one of the bigger shortfalls in the league, and one goal in his last ten on 5.7. Goals tend to follow chances like that. Recently he's been scoring on the power play, which is the role change paying off.

The Kings take 57% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, 11 points better than without him, on a team stuck at 5-9-2. A third-round pick out of Harvard, he scored 21 goals last season. Our range has him at 18 to 32 goals.
